correctness.rationale: Direct cosine integration proves the piecewise formulas; large amplitude strict descent follows from the positive arcsine-density integral. The derivative sign reduces to K(t) compared with m/(1-m), and P derivative is -4t alpha(t), proving one fold. The stationary height ratio R has derivative -P(t)(alpha(t)+t s(t))/(2 pi s(t)t^2 alpha(t)^2), so the unique first-order equality and all boundary counts follow globally. The current package checker independently numerically tests formulas and constants (101 assertions); it does not establish the infinite quantifiers.

equivalent_formulations.reasoning: A general Jensen sign is not equivalent: the untruncated quadratic always declines in amplitude. The abrupt optimum depends on leaving the viability interval while the mean stays strictly within it. No equivalent exact closed-form amplitude phase diagram was found, but non-detection is not a novelty certificate.

originality.rationale: The claimed discontinuous amplitude switch and separate fold concern a clipped quadratic under a fixed interior mean. Full accessible versions of the 2008 thermal-preference and 2013 rate-summation studies address different optimization variables and empirically fitted functions, respectively; 2011 and 2015 studies supply related empirical evidence without an identified analytic equivalence. Earlier accessible interior/thermal results do not imply the two thresholds; priority is provisional against general mathematical convolution work.
residual_risks: General mathematical arcsine-convolution, truncated-polynomial expectation, or parametric global optimization literature may imply the specialized phase diagram.
2011 and 2015 biological research was only inspected at abstract level; neither is dismissed as ruled out on that basis.
Earlier exterior-mean result uses exactly the same instant response but cannot imply the interior-mean switching theorem; this is a meaningful extension, not a disjoint physical application.

value.rationale: Mathematically motivated thermal-rate averaging exhibits a discontinuous optimal variance amplitude at an interior mean and a separate fold producing a metastable local optimum. This exact structural boundary is not the textbook Jensen calculation for a concave untruncated quadratic and offers a benchmark for assessing hard thermal cutoffs under variable conditions, with no empirical universality claimed.
